I worked at McDonald's for three years, and worked up from a lowly crew member to department manager in training before I decided to quit for an internship with the Department of Defense. AMA
IAmA ex-McDonalds manager who quit just recently. AMA

How did you project your experience at McDonald's into value during the interview for your new internship?

How do you move up the ladder at a franchise like McDonald's?

What was your most positive customer experience?

That was the most difficult. I eventually decided the best way to project my experiences as a value to the DOD in a multitude of ways. First, I can lead a team. Managing McDonalds is not easy: you have to control a team of people who don't care or hate their jobs (on average, not all do) into a cohesive unit, that works together to create a great experience for the customer. I also have to look at minor details and explain why its actually a big deal to the employees. I can be in compromising situations, where my life is threatened (yes), and where people project their hated onto me. This all improved my skills that will be necessary for this new position.

You move up by working hard, and caring. Even if the job isn't amazingly challenging, you need to work like it is the most important thing at that time. Seniority doesn't matter, as I had less time at McDonald's than many of my coworkers and was promoted before them. Work hard, show your value, and it will be returned.

My most positive customer experience is from our recurring customers. One guy, let's name him John, comes in every day for a sweet tea. He cracks a sarcastic joke (I suck with sarcasm) and I take it completely serious. He looks at me dumbfounded, and another employee says, 'pivotraze, that was a joke." I then look at the customer, and the conversation follows:

"Have you ever watched The Big Bang Theory?" "Yes..." "I'm like Sheldon." John starts laughing and says, "'pivotraze, I like you!"

From then on, he called me Sheldon, and always treated me with a lot of respect. My last day, he shook my hand, and wished me best of luck.
What is the biggest reason not to eat at McDonalds, other than reasons related to health?

Quality. Employees don't always care, and food quality will suffer. Sandwiches will be made sloppy, food will sit longer than it should. Nobody will spit in your food (firing offense). Food is never really unsafe, as management is very careful with that. But is it tasty always? No. It should be, but not everyone cares.
Spitting in someone's food is also illegal in many jurisdictions.
In my county, it was a reason to shut down a food place. We were very careful. Passed all our health inspection with flying colors.

I hid boogers under pepperoni slices when I was a delivery driver in college. This dude lived on the 18th floor of a privately owned student housing complex for rich kids and NEVER tipped. Delivering there sucked because it took forever to get up and down the elevators (stopped at every damn floor), meaning you not only lost out on the tip this cheap fuck didn't give you, but tips you would have earned delivering instead of waiting for/riding elevators. Only time I ever boogered a pizza. Asshole was also always smoking out, and never offered pizza guy a hit.

McDonalds has recently been investing a lot of money and time into the Our Food. Your Questions campaign. They even had Grant Imahara from Mythbusters (ex) do several videos "busting" food myths. Personally, I give a lot of respect to McDonalds for doing this and even answering some hard hitting questions about the quality of their food.

What are you thoughts on these videos and answers? Do you know if these videos are really opening the curtain on the behind the scenes of the food preparation processes?

I also like the videos. I was really happy when they explained the campaign to us. I was excited for what it will show our guests. When they go to the manufacturing, I can't guarantee it. However, from what I have seen it is generally accurate. Food is cooked like they show in the video, and is generally spot on. I haven't seen any blatant lies or white lies on the in-store process. I hope that answers you enough. If not, ask some more questions and I'll do my best to answer them (:
What's one of the worst customers you've ever had to deal with?

Well, I'll choose the absolute worst.

I received a call stating a lady ordered one snack wrap and paid for two in drive thru. Over the headset, I remember hearing her asking for two. So, I tell her I will gladly refund the second snack wrap if she comes into town. The response? "That's it? That is all you are going to do?" I realize she wants free food for buying more than she can eat. I reply "I'm sorry, there isn't much more I can do."

She responded in the most calm headed and obvious manner: "I hope you and your family dies." And then hangs up.
Woah, she took it a bit too far. I can understand that she was clearly upset, but there's no reason anything like that should be wished upon anyone. Especially over a few dollars..
Wow man that's crazy, were incidents like this common?

From another former McD's employee: We had this lady who refused to pay for her shake since I forgot to ring it up with the rest of her food. She started screaming and throwing a fit and demanded a free shake. We just gave her a free shake.
Do you think that the cashiers deserve $15 an hour for their efforts? I'm not trying to start shit, I'm genuinely curious

No. Why should we (I guess its no longer me though ha-ha!) Make more than soldiers? EMTs? Our job isn't hard enough for that much. As a manager, I made $10.50. Enough for what I did? No. Worth $15? No. As a manager, $12 or $13 an hour is fair. As an employee? I'd say no more than $10 personally.

Well the point of raising to $15 an hour is better living quality, $10 simply doesn't make it nowadays.

I guess it's largely dependent on where you live however. The McDonalds next to my work actually starts employees at $12 an hr.
If you raise minimum wage, prices go up. We recently put our minimum at $8.55/hr (state minimum is $8.05). Price increases occurred across the board.

I've heard that in some areas, you can find it easy to become blacklisted from moving up in the company. People that would turn down promotions to management levels because they didn't want to change stores would find themselves being passed up for future opportunities sometimes years later. Have you come across anything like this?

Also, yay or nay on the McRib?

Sort of. Past employees can end up on a "no-hire" list due to past performance. They will never get another job at amy of the organization's McDonald's again. But from being promoted? No. I've never seen that.

Yay to McRib if you remove slivered onions and pickles, add diced/recon onions and white cheddar cheese (I used to add swiss, but swiss is no more sadly.)
OMG. I love the diced onions. Everyone thinks I'm crazy, but I love those little dehydrated things.
Will you encourage your children not to eat at McDonald's?
Depends on what he wants. Some of it is healthy. Not most of it. Will he get happy meals? No.
Would you personally eat the McLobster? Something about it terrifies me.
ABSOLUTELY NOT! That thing looked like puke on a bun. I wouldn't touch that with a ten foot pole!

I've seen signs in McDonald's advertising something of a McDonald's management school or something like that and how it gives you career direction and such. Is this still a thing and have you used it? Is it more than just an online course?

I haven't seen advertisements for it. There are two. LMS for crew trainers to store managers. It is online training, with mixed in coaching sessions. There is also Hamburger University for store managers and the like. It is an actual university. I think a week long. I haven't attended HU, but LMS and a few actual sit down classes, yes. I attended Introduction to Management. A required course for all managers, as well as SIO (Shift Into Overdrive) which is a recommended class that our owner requires.

I used to work at McDonalds prior to their implementation of using clamshells and storing meats in bins after they are cooked. I feel like this has led to the downfall of quality in taste of the product. All the juices end up in the bin, where they sit waiting.

When I worked there, they went straight from the grill to the bun, and the burgers were much better.

OK here is my question...Can I order one "Off the grill", if I come in and am ready to wait a few minutes? Do people do this at all? I know at Burger King, you can request for one "off the broiler", and it tastes twice as good.
By bin do you mean trays? If so, yeah juices do run :/ yes you can! We had it often.

Trays/Bins, whatever. Those things have ruined the food there. I worked there in the late 80's, early 90's, and the food was so much better. We cracked eggs for the folded eggs as well as the round. Cooked them on the grill. The wait times are what forced the changeover, i guess.

Policy was to make whole batches of burgers/Quarter Pounders at once. Put everything on them, and they would sit in a warmer up front. If you wanted a double or special things done to the burger, it would have to be made fresh. This could cause a massive problem in the drive through. I worked there during the Mc DLT days as well. This is why In and out is so popular (and tasty) as they come hot off the grill to you.

The fries and biscuits still rock, though. And I have to have a fliet o' fish once a month. Freaking comfort food for me, hah.

Yeah. Quality is lower :/ wait times is a huge priority now. Policy is not to make entire sandwiches now, just the patties place them in the UHC (Universal Holding Cabinet). All sandwiches are made to order now. I think most of our food is outstanding when made right.

Double Filet-O-Fish guy here. Sub white cheddar!
Do you cook the Veggie burger patties on the same grill as the meat patties?
This one I can't answer. Our stores don't have veggie burgers, but I'm going to wager no.
Yeah they don't have them in Australia as well, but I have had them in other countries such as the UK. Thanks for quick response
Why is a double chee plain so delicious?
Perfectly seasoned meat, freshly toasted bun, and deliciously melted cheese can do that ;)
Do you think Franchising is a good business model for people who want to own their own business?

Absolutely! It gives you policies and practices, as well as procedures that are tried and succeed. It also instantly gives brand recognition. However, if you want to truly do it your own way, it is not. Corporate comes to every store at some point and ensures it is done their way.
How many candidates did you get for an open position? How did you vet them?

Easily hundreds. We sort through hundreds of applications every time.

An application goes through corporate first for a background check. Then it comes to the owner who does extra checks (our stores don't hire people who are homeless, which frustrated me when some seemed so dedicated to turning their life around). After they approve it, it goes to the store manager who calls them and has an in-person interview to ensure they are right for the store. It seems like easy questions, but we are trained to not only listen to the answers, but read body language and how the voice sounds during the answers.

McDonalds doesn't hire people who are homeless? Is this a chain-wide policy?

Also, did you prefer to hire friendly people? What qualities were you looking for?

Just an organization policy. It was ridiculous and made me extemeely mad. I even placed myself as a reference for the guy (I talked to him for a long time about his life and his wanted future) but he didn't get the job.

Yes, generally friendlier. Personality is a huge hiring point, even if it can be faked. Be friendly and nice at EVERY point after applying and jt will help if we do interview You. Not everyone who gets to an interview gets the job.
I'm interested in the homeless thing, as well. Is it an administrative thing because they don't have a permanent address? Is it because it is difficult to maintain a standard of cleanliness?
Did you work at one of the McDonald's with a kids' play area? Did you ever shine a black light around that area?

We had a crappy version. A turtle, a tree, a car, a log bridge thing. It was sad. But no, I never did. I'd say you wouldn't find much? It is scrubbed every night with a deck scrub brush, sanitizing spray, and special mop liquid. I hope nothing would show...
I didn't expect that it would be cleaned so often! I'm impressed.

Yeah :) we closed playland at 9pm and took about 1.5 hours cleaning it all. It sucks. You know the music that plays in there? We aren't allowed to shut it off so I always feel bad for the poor sucker who has to clean it :p
What are some secrets/loopholes people can take advantage of? :P

Found a McDonald's receipt within the last three days somewhere? We messed up your food. Call in, have receipt ready. Some managers will require food brought back in. Don't excessively do it, we keep track of repeat callers. Before I left I was developing software specifically for this. Finished it, but we couldn't use it because we don't have full access to the system. I hope competitors like it.
Can you tell more about McDonalds quality standards in overseas regions,particularly developing regions of Asia

I haven't been told too much about it, but from what I've heard, it isn't too different from America. Same standards, but in some countries, they will spit in foreigners food. Obviously not policy. But pure hatred.
That is real bad. What crap mindset can some people have that they can't appreciate people from other countries. Very sad.
I was shocked when I heard it. That's a horrible thing to do!
How do you feel about some McDonalds replacing cashiers with an electronic terminal?
While it makes perfect sense, I am saddened. Many people will lose a job, but it will increase profits. I think one or two people should be retained to help customers type in orders. At least.
Has McDonald's ever discouraged you or someone you know from forming or participating in a union?
Nope. Retaliation is not allowed at McDonald's. Everyone at my stores didn't want a union so no one ever participated in any protests.
Is social media an issue? Is there a policy you have to agree to about posting vids/pics while on duty or in uniform?
Yes! We had multiple serious issues involving social media and cyberbullying. There is a online acceptance policy one has to sign.
